# PWR Subject Notes

The knowledge in the coursework archive that has no repository, written down — plus the census
that proves nothing was quietly left out. Ten notes, one generated index over **73 subject
entries / 48,815 files / 11 GB**, four scripts.

## The problem it solves

An archive of eight semesters does not divide cleanly into things worth building and things
worth forgetting. Subjects with a runnable artefact became repositories; most subjects do not
have one, and earlier passes handled that by leaving them out. The result was a coverage claim
that was true about the repositories and silent about everything else.

The rule here: **every subject folder gets a disposition, and an exclusion is never silent.**

## The census names its own gaps

`scripts/census.py` walks the archive and prints, by name, every subject folder for which no
disposition has been recorded. That is the check — not a sentence in a README claiming
completeness. It is [[census-that-names-its-own-gaps]], and it is the same shape as
[[verify-the-load-dont-declare-it]] and [[generated-audit-artifact]] applied to coverage rather
than to data or documentation.

`INDEX.md` is generated by it. Editing the numbers by hand is not how it is updated.

**It also resolves what it prints.** A row reading `note: linux-laboratory` is checked against
`notes/`, a row reading `repo: Physics` against the sibling directories, and every note file
must be named by at least one row. Added 2026-08-05 after an audit found this repository's own
README claiming **nine** notes while `notes/` held **ten** — never true, since the first commit
contained ten, and invisible because nothing counted them. Checking both directions is the
point: a missing target is a broken row, and only an orphan note catches a count that has moved.

**Re-running it writes nothing when nothing has moved.** It used to stamp today's date into
`INDEX.md`, so running the check dirtied the artefact the check was about. The date now means
*when these numbers last changed*, and a clean `git status` after a census run is itself the
evidence — the same move as reporting two numbers in the integrity script below.

## Three things it found

**A census that walks subdirectories misses this archive.** `2nd Semester` has no subject
folders at all — 116 files sit loose at its root, including the only operating-systems
coursework in the archive that is not a screenshot. An earlier pass counted subdirectories and
reported 80 folders and 16,066 files; counting loose files at every semester root gives 54,034.
Neither figure was dishonest. The first excluded what it could not classify and did not say so,
which is [[documentation-drift]] in a measurement rather than in prose.

**Four "unverified mapping" rows were checkable in one pass.** `7th/TP` was filed as *teaching
material without an assessed artefact* and is in fact the requirements specification for
[[health-awareness-support-platform]]. `4th semester/Sys lab` was filed as unverified and its two
CSV files are the inputs of [[air-quality-public-health-analysis]]. A folder name is a
hypothesis; checking it moved four subjects from unknown to covered — and `5th/MAAP` from
assumed-covered to genuinely missing.

**An exclusion by association excluded real work.** `6th/SADiSM` was excluded from an earlier
matrix because Bishop and Murphy sit in that folder. Excluding the textbooks was right; the four
laboratory specifications and three completed solution trees beside them were excluded without
being named. That folder is now [[systems-analysis-and-decision-support]].

## What the notes are for

Not summaries of lecture material. Each says what a subject covered, what in it is worth
carrying forward, and what was decided about it — including the decisions to build nothing:

- `linux-laboratory.md` — 320 terminal screenshots, and why rebuilding them into a shell script
  destroys the artefact rather than preserving it.
- `software-engineering-scope-boundary.md` — three folders and 1.6 M characters that would have
  become a third copy of [[information-systems-modelling]]. The note narrows the scope to the one
  thing no existing repository does: requirements traceability, pointed at a real SRS and the
  system that implements it.
- `unclassified-and-duplicate-folders.md` — the four folders holding most of the archive by size,
  each unresolved in a different way, each counted rather than dropped.
- `advanced-web-technologies-and-engineering-ethics.md` — the counterweight. Everything else in
  this archive rests on checkable claims; the ethics notes are the one subject that cannot be
  tested and would misrepresent the education if omitted.

## Proving the archive is intact

`verify_archive_untouched.sh` checks the immutability claim rather than asserting it, and
reports two numbers because they are different claims. In the prior archive snapshot, **94 files** under `5th/MAAP` carry
modification times after the freeze — every one a `.git` index or `.gradle` lock refreshed by
inspection tooling — and **zero content files** changed.

"Nothing was touched" and "no content was touched" are not the same statement, and only the
second one is true. Collapsing them into one reassuring number is the failure this script exists
to avoid — [[provenance-and-limits-stated-inline]].

## What is deliberately absent

The ~33 million characters of extracted lecture text are a working cache and are committed
nowhere: that text is the lecturers' expression. Four third-party textbooks are named and were
not opened, including a 688-page pirated JEE algebra text watermarked *"downloaded from
jeemain.guru"* on every page, found inside the algebra exercise folder. Personal, financial and
assessment records are counted in the census and appear nowhere else — [[provenance-notice-file]].

## 2026-08-12 reference audit

With the current configured PWR archive root, the census passed and regenerated its index at
**73 entries / 48,815 files / 11 GB / 10 notes**, with all 73 entries carrying a stated
disposition. The coverage chart regenerated from that index and was idempotent on a second
run. The timestamp-based integrity check found **zero files** newer than the documented
freeze, hence zero newer content files. The default archive paths in both check scripts now
match the located archive; the WSL-provided `bash` cannot access Windows drive paths, so that
timestamp result was verified with PowerShell using the script's same subject and exclusion
rules.

## Status

Committed locally on `main`. No remote. The census is re-runnable and is the way this page's
figures should be refreshed.
